nodes.title: A test called the campaigns dispatcher tick() without a workspaceId. On the shared CI database that dispatcher claimed attempts that belonged to another test file running in parallel.
nodes.broke: At 2f32449 the WIP e2e test called tick({ pool, registry, now }) with no workspaceId. It claimed the campaigns double-claim test's attempts, so campaigns saw 3 of 5 claimed and e2e dispatched 3 instead of 2. Both failures looked like load contention and were first reported as flakes. 7e998c0 scopes every tick to the e2e workspace. product/ARCHITECTURE.md now says that any test driving a worker or a job body passes its own workspaceId.

nodes.title: The 12-worker / 5-attempt claim race test (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) passes every time under load once nothing outside its workspace claims rows: 0 failures in 205 runs.
nodes.method: node --test --test-name-pattern 'double claim' tests/campaigns.test.ts on a throwaway Postgres 16 in the 4-vCPU sandbox. 15 runs with 4 busy-loop processes saturating the CPU, then 190 runs while intake-scale (50k rows) imported into the same database.

events.event: CI root cause: the campaigns and e2e failures were cross-file claims, not load
events.details: An unscoped dispatcher tick in the WIP e2e test (2f32449) claimed other files' attempts; 7e998c0 fixed it. The intake-scale 5,000-row default still goes ahead because it cuts CI time.
